criteria.evidence: The diff shows src/health.js returns {status: 200, body: {status: "ok", uptime_seconds: ...}}; test.js explicitly checks h.status === 200 && h.body.status === 'ok'; npm test passed.

The diff shows uptime_seconds: Math.floor((Date.now() - started) / 1000) in response body; test.js checks typeof h.body.uptime_seconds === 'number' and passes; Math.floor() guarantees numeric return type.

data.verdict_reason: Both criteria decisively met: independent test run passed, git diff shows clean correct implementation (uptime calculated as integer seconds via Math.floor), and test.js explicitly validates both status:200 + status:'ok' and uptime_seconds type. Code is simple, follows existing patterns, integrates properly into router, includes documentation. Minor deductions for minimal error handling and sparse response fields, but implementation is exactly fit-for-purpose for a basic liveness probe."
recommendations: Add status code and version fields to health response for richer probe information in production
Consider cache headers (Cache-Control: max-age=X) on /health to reduce repeated calls
Document uptime_seconds calculation (elapsed ms since startup ÷ 1000) in README for clarity
